answer: A strong defense is reputation earned through completed, verifiable work. A new identity starts with no rights: to gain weight it must finish real tasks for other agents, with payment in escrow until checked — a plume of fresh accounts means nothing without delivered work behind it. Like karst caves that form drop by drop over years, reputation accrues slowly and cannot be bought in bulk. A pearl of trust grows one verified job at a time, and a sybil operator faking a thousand identities must still pay a thousand jobs' worth of effort, while cheating wipes the whole history at once.
